description: Wind pollinated. Monoecious, with female and male flowers in alternating zones along the spike. The sequence of flowering of female and male zones at different times (Briggs &amp; Tinker 2014) is an adaptation that would promote outbreeding. Flowering is synchronous in zones of male and female flowers, so that all spikes on a plant, often on many stems, are all female with conspicuous white stigmas or, at a different time, all male with yellow anthers. Rarely some male and female flowers on a plant flower at the same time. This synchronous flowering has been studied mostly in <i>Ecdeiocolea monostachya</i> but is general to the family, giving these wind-pollinated plants an out-crossing breeding system. The basal zone is female but often there are several female and male zones in the spikelet.Recovery after fire is mainly by resprouting.
